hypotheses.reasoning: redis-cache restarted after node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it started with 0 keys (#157, 13:03:17). Requests were healthy right up to that point (~100ms 200s). Straight after, search-api's cache miss ratio jumped to 94-97% and every miss went to catalog-db (#158, #163). That pushed catalog-db to 490/500 connections and 99% CPU (#162), with simple primary-key lookups slowing to 3-8s (#164, #226). search-api queries on products then timed out after 5s (#171, #202, #219), and web-bff returned 504s to clients. The trigger was small and survivable on its own (a cold cache); the damage came from every cache miss hitting the database at once.
catalog-db is close to its connection limit and CPU is pegged. But that started only after the cache went cold, so it reads as a symptom, not the origin.
index-worker v3.9.2 rolled out at 12:54, 8 minutes before onset. index-worker kept processing normally and isn't on the /search request path, so this is unlikely.

verdict.recommendedAction: Shed load or rate-limit cache-miss reads to catalog-db, and warm redis-cache with the hot product keys. Add request coalescing (single-flight) or locking on cache misses in search-api, plus jittered TTLs. Turn on RDB/AOF persistence or a replica so a node replacement doesn't bring the cache back empty. Consider adding catalog-db read replicas.
